one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is fiscal Q1 FY27 earnings (quarter ended 2026-10-02). No date is announced, but the precedents are Oct 26 2023, Oct 22 2024 and Oct 28 2025, so the report very likely (~90%) lands before Nov 1. Guidance is $4.1B +/- $0.1B revenue and $7.30 +/- $0.20 non-GAAP EPS. Seagate has beaten through this cycle, so a beat is likely. The stock will trade on the Q2 guide and on what management says about CY2028 pricing (volume is allocated into 2028, but prices are contracted only for CY2027) and Toshiba. The July print showed a two-sided reaction (about -8% on the day, then a rebound). The second input is the -11% sector drop on Oct 2 on the Nikkei Toshiba report. The two earlier >10% one-day sector drops this year (June, July 2) were partly retraced within weeks, which supports a small upward drift. I centre at about $845 (+1%) with a 20% one-month sigma, slightly under the 75%/3.5 = 21% rule because realized vol already includes several earnings and shock days. Unchanged from round 1: the supervisor's findings concern CY2028 and debt, and neither changes the one-month picture.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (scenario-weighted NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $46 x 16.5x = $759, plus ~$7/share net cash = $766) and FCF yield (~$40.5/share at 5.25% = $771, plus net cash = $778), weighted 60/40, giving about $770 one year out.

Toshiba adds about +3-6% to industry exabytes by end-CY2027 (11% share, MAMR-only until FY2028 HAMR, outside heads/media; its 2022 doubling plan left share unchanged), against demand growing in the mid-20s %. WD has top-customer terms into 2028-29 and hyperscalers prioritise supply assurance, which argues against price cuts. But in past cycles (2019, 2022-23) price per TB rolled over within 1-2 years of a supply response, so a 30% chance of flat or down CY2028 pricing is my base rate.

FY27 about $33 (Q1 $7.30 rising ~$0.5 a quarter to a Q4 run-rate of ~$8.8). NTM at Oct-2027 is about half CY2027-priced and half CY2028-priced. Cases: flat/down pricing gives ~$38 (run-rate plus volume growth only); +5-10% pricing gives ~$47; strong pricing gives ~$55 (the consensus reference). Weighted 0.3/0.5/0.2 = $45.9.

About 24x FY27 at today's price. HDD peak-cycle multiples were 8-15x (2018, 2022 per price history). Contracted CY2027 pricing and allocated CY2028 volume justify a premium to that history, but by Oct-2027 the market will be pricing a likely earnings peak with CY2028 prices open.

227M outstanding at July 3 plus 1.65M from the exchangeable settlement; the convert dilution in the 231M Q1 guide has ended.

Above a typical large-cap tech yield (3-4%) for a cyclical product with open CY2028 pricing; below the 8-12% yields STX traded at in past troughs. Slightly tighter than round 1's 5.5% because a 2027 recession is now priced at only ~22% on Kalshi.

bear.story: The usual storage-cycle ending, delayed by the CY2027 contracts. Toshiba and WDC add capacity, hyperscaler capex pauses in 2027, and CY2028 LTAs settle flat to down per exabyte. The market takes NTM EPS toward $36 and pays ~12x (about -46%, close to the 2018 -44% and 2022 -60% peak-to-trough drawdowns). Weight is a bit below my 30% chance of flat/down CY2028 pricing: flat pricing on its own leaves EPS near $38 and does not by itself produce a bust; that also needs a capex or recession shock, now priced at ~22% on Kalshi.

base.story: Seagate delivers FY27 EPS of about $33-35 and signs CY2028 contracts at modest price increases (+5-10%). The multiple compresses from ~24x FY27 to ~16-17x NTM as the market prices peak-cycle earnings. The stock ends near today's level after large swings.

bull.story: AI inference and data retention keep exabyte demand growth above 25-30%. Toshiba's ramp is absorbed (MAMR-only until FY2028 HAMR, head/media limited, as with its 2022 plan), CY2028 contracts reprice up strongly, and Mozaic 4/5 lift margins. NTM EPS is above $60 and the market pays ~22x.

thesis_break_reason: About $510 (-39%) is ~11x my $46 NTM EPS, a peak-cycle multiple. Below it the market would be pricing an actual break in the CY2028 contract-pricing thesis: flat or falling price per exabyte in new LTAs, hyperscaler build-to-order deferrals, a Mozaic slip or a guide-down. That would not be a sentiment drop on a competitor headline like Oct 2. The 2026 one-day sector shocks bottomed around $700-760.

reasoning: Round 2 revisions follow the supervisor's checks. (1) I wrote 'sold out at fixed prices into 2028', which overstated the call: pricing is contracted only through CY2027. So I no longer haircut a single consensus number. I built NTM EPS at Oct-2027 from the guided FY27 path plus CY2028 pricing cases weighted 30/50/20, which gives $46 (was $50); the $55.37 consensus is now only the bull reference. (2) Debt is ~$2.4B, not $3.6B, so I add ~$7/share of net cash at the horizon instead of subtracting net debt. Shares are ~229M. (3) I pulled the Kalshi 2027 recession market directly from its public API: KXRECSSNBER-27 last traded at 22c (bid 20 / ask 22, volume ~$542k, OI ~275k), not the 41% I quoted from an aggregator. Its definition is two negative GDP quarters, a narrower bar than an NBER recession. (4) As the supervisor suggested, I conditioned the cycle base rate: the 2018 (-44%) and 2022 (-60%) drawdowns started after pricing had rolled over, while CY2027 pricing is contracted now. I tied the bust weight to my 30% chance of flat/down CY2028 pricing times the chance of a demand shock, and lowered it from 25% to 22%. The net effect on fair value is small and slightly negative ($795 -> $770): less EPS, partly offset by net cash and a slightly tighter FCF yield. I disagree with the supervisor's 17x / $47: with CY2028 pricing open and the stock at a likely earnings peak, I stay at 16-16.5x. The ladder is a mixture of 78% lognormal (median $865, sigma 0.47) and 22% bust (median $560, sigma 0.60). I widened the main sigma from 0.42 to 0.47: for a stock with 75% trailing vol that went $212 to $1,145 in a year, my round-1 right tail (P(>=2094) = 1.6%) was too thin. P(>= spot) is about 47% and the scenario mean is about $870, so the distribution is right-skewed with a fat cyclical left tail. Research this round was about 4 queries plus one direct API pull. WD's top-customer terms into 2028-29 support volume but say nothing about price.
